awd_titl_txt: Travel: NSF Student Travel Grant for the 2025 IEEE North American School of Information Theory (NASIT 2025)
awd_abstract_narration:
The 2025 IEEE North American School for Information Theory (NASIT 2025) will be held at the University of Minnesota in Minneapolis, from June 16th to June 20th, 2025. This grant provides support for the expenses of school participants from the United States such as graduate students and  postdoctoral fellows. Attendees will benefit by learning from senior colleagues, presenting their own research in poster sessions, and expanding their network with the research community. This award will cover accommodation and travel for students.

The IEEE North American School (NAS) for Information Theory is an annual event of the IEEE Information Theory Society; 2025 will be the 17th year the school will have held the event. The NAS provides a supportive environment where foundations for learning and long-term future scientific collaborations are established. NAS delivers interactive education for graduate students in mathematics, engineering, and computer sciences. It presents students the opportunity to meet and learn from senior researchers in academia and industry who present long-format tutorials. Student and postdoctoral participants present their research results in poster sessions.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This award supported part of the costs for participants in the 2025 IEEE North American School of Information Theory, hosted at the University of Minnesota from June 16 to June 20, 2025. This was the 17th annual offering of the school, which is one of the premier educational events covering information theory, coding theory, and related areas.

The school aims to provide students and postdoctoral researchers with opportunities to:

  • Learn from senior lecturers through tutorials;

  • Participate in a stimulating and collaborative forum of scientists;

  • Present their own research and receive feedback for potential collaboration; and

  • Strengthen their connections within the information theory community.

At the 2025 school, several leading researchers delivered both long tutorials (3 hours) and shorter lectures (1.5 hours) on the applications of information theory and coding theory in wireless communications, machine learning, optimization, privacy, and bioinformatics. The speakers were: Viveck Cadambe (Georgia Institute of Technology), Sanghamitra Dutta (University of Maryland), Elza Erkip (New York University), Gauri Joshi (Carnegie Mellon University), Nihar Shah (Carnegie Mellon University), Ilan Shomorony (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign), Mahdi Soltanolkotabi (University of Southern california), Ali Tajer (Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Emre Telatar (Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne), Ramya Vinayak (University of Wisconsin), and Qian Yu (University of California, Santa Barbara).

The lectures were professionally recorded and are available on the website of the school.

The event brought together 66 participants, including PhD students and postdoctoral researchers, who attended tutorials, expanded their professional networks, and presented their own research in two poster sessions.

The school was organized by Martina Cardone, Mohammad Maddah-Ali, and Soheil Mohajer from the University of Minnesota as general chairs, Shirin Jalali from Rutgers University as financial chair, and Shirin Saeedi Bidokhti and Hamed Hassani from the University of Pennsylvania as advisors.

Additional details and lecture materials from the event can be found on the school's website: https://sites.google.com/umn.edu/nasit-2025/home.
